_comment: Copy this file to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global) or .cursor/mcp.json (per-project). Replace <ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_THIS_REPO>. The other servers under _optional are commented-out templates kept here for the day this project grows beyond local files.

filesystem-research._comment: The only server actually required for this repo. Exposes ./data/ (transcripts, survey CSV, schemas, alignment) read-only so Cursor can grep, summarize, and quote across the qualitative + quantitative corpora.

_optional_future_servers._note: These are NOT active. Copy any of them into mcpServers above (and fill in placeholders) only if/when this project gains a warehouse or a paid product. See README §FAQ.

bigquery._comment: Add a warehouse for telemetry once n > a few hundred. Pair with a fresh schema doc at data/schemas/bigquery_<dataset>.md.

stripe._comment: Only if/when the EdTech product starts charging. Restricted READ-ONLY key strongly recommended.

posthog._comment: Only if you ship a client app and start collecting product events.

security: The filesystem server is read-only by default in the @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem package — it cannot delete or modify files.
Interview transcripts contain identifying language (names, employer, child age, location). Treat the contents of ./data/ as confidential research material.
If you ever uncomment the BigQuery / Stripe / PostHog blocks: use read-only credentials, set --max-bytes-billed for BigQuery, and never commit the filled-in config.
verification: After saving, restart Cursor and open Settings → MCP. `filesystem-research` should show a green status dot.
If it's red, run the exact command from `command` + `args` in your terminal to see the stderr.
